title: Ex Vivo Mouse Brain Slice Whole-Cell Patch-Clamp Electrophysiology
author: Andrew Miller-Hansen
materials: ACSF for recovery and recordings contained in mM: 125 NaCl, 26 NaHCO3, 1.25 NaH2PO4, 2.5 KCl, 1 MgCl2, 2 CaCl2, 11 Glucose. For recordings, picrotoxin (50 μM, Sigma) was added.
After fully dissolving, filter the solution twice using a 0.22 µm membrane filter (e.g., MilliporeSigma‱).

steps.title: Prepare slicing and internal solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 1× ACSF and NMDG slicing solution daily with (mM): 92 NMDG, 2.5 KCl, 1.2 NaH₂PO₄, 30 NaHCO₃, 20 HEPES, 25 Glucose, 5 Na‑Ascorbate, 2 Thiourea, 3 Na‑Pyruvate, 10 MgSO₄, 0.5 CaCl₂ (Millipore Sigma); continuously bubble with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂ to keep pH 7.4 and osmolarity 300‑305 mOsm. Prepare either a Cs‑based internal solution (mM: 117 CsMeSO₃, 2.8 NaCl, 0.4 EGTA, 20 HEPES, 4 Mg‑ATP, 0.3 Na₃‑GTP, 5 QX‑314 Cl, 5 TEA‑Cl, 0.1 Spermine 4HCl) or a K‑based internal solution (mM: 135 KMeSO₃, 5 KCl, 10 HEPES, 4 Mg‑ATP, 0.3 Na₃‑GTP, 8 Na₂‑phosphocreatine, 1 EGTA, 0.1 CaCl₂). Adjust each internal solution to pH 7.3‑7.4 with CsOH (for Cs‑based) or KOH (for K‑based) and osmolarity 280‑290 mOsm. Aliquot solutions (≈100 µL per tube) and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Anesthetize and perfuse animal
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice according to approved Animal Care and Use Committee protocols, then transcardially perfuse with ice‑cold N‑Methyl‑D‑Glucamine (NMDG) solution.

steps.title: Extract brain and begin slicing
steps.instruction: Decapitate the animal, quickly extract the brain, and submerge it in ice‑cold ACSF or an optimized cutting solution (e.g., high‑sucrose, low‑sodium).

steps.title: Cut coronal brain slices
steps.instruction: Using a vibratome (e.g., Leica VT1200s), cut 300 µm‑thick coronal slices that contain the region of interest.

steps.title: Set up recording chamber
steps.instruction: Transfer a slice to a recording chamber, secure it with an anchor (e.g., Warner Instrument), and start ACSF perfusion at 2‑3 mL/min at 30 °C. Mount the chamber on a microscope (e.g., Olympus BX51) equipped with a Multiclamp 700B amplifier (Molecular Devices) and monitor recordings with custom MATLAB software (MathWorks) or other software such as Wavesurfer or WinWCP V5.7.

steps.title: Prepare patch pipettes
steps.instruction: Pull glass pipettes to a resistance of 2.5‑5 MΩ using a micropipette puller (e.g., Narishige PC‑100 or Sutter P‑97) and fill them with the appropriate internal solution (Cs‑based or K‑based).

steps.title: Form seal and achieve whole‑cell mode
steps.instruction: Apply positive pressure (~5 Kp) to the pipette while approaching the target cell; upon contact, release pressure to form a giga‑ohm seal. Hold the membrane at –70 mV and apply brief negative pressure to break in and obtain whole‑cell configuration.

steps.title: Apply pharmacology and set holding potentials
steps.instruction: If measuring AMPA rectification, wash the slice in D‑AP5 (50 µM, Tocris). Hold the cell at –70 mV for excitatory postsynaptic currents (AMPAR‑mediated), at +40 mV for combined NMDAR/AMPAR currents, or at 0 mV for inhibitory postsynaptic currents (GABAergic) as required.

steps.title: Acquire and filter data
steps.instruction: Low‑pass filter the recorded signal at 2.2 kHz and digitize at 10 kHz (e.g., using a National Instruments NI PCIe‑6259 card or comparable digitizer). Exclude any cell with series resistance greater than 25 MΩ from analysis.
